subject: Baltic Sea
hook: BALTIC SEA IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: The Baltic Sea is named the 'East Sea' by almost every surrounding Germanic and Finnic culture, while the name 'Baltic' is primarily a convention used by English speakers and Romance-language nations.
angle_support: In Germanic languages, except English, 'East Sea' is used, as in Afrikaans (Oossee), Danish (Østersøen), Dutch (Oostzee), German (Ostsee), and Swedish (Östersjön).
In addition, Finnish, a Finnic language, uses the term Itämeri 'East Sea', possibly a calque from a Germanic language.
title: Why the Baltic Sea has different names
description: The name Baltic is primarily a convention used by English and Romance-language speakers. Most cultures bordering the sea use names like East Sea or West Sea based on their own geography.
narration: BALTIC SEA IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a singular name etched on every world map. It was closer to a localized disagreement, as most surrounding cultures reject the term entirely for their own. While English and Romance languages use the label Baltic, German, Danish, Swedish, and Finnish speakers overwhelmingly identify it as the East Sea. Estonian speakers uniquely call it the West Sea, reflecting their own distinct coastal geography. The name depends entirely on where you happen to be standing.
